blocks.h2: How We Install a Gas Line

steps.body: With a shutoff at each appliance.

blocks.intro: Algonquin homeowners invest in their homes, and gas lines are a common upgrade.

items.h3: Outdoor Living Is the Big Driver
items.body: Most gas line calls we get from Algonquin are for patios and backyards: grills, fire pits and heaters.
Original gas lines in 1990s and 2000s homes were sized for the furnace, water heater and maybe a range. Adding several outdoor appliances can need a larger line.
We plan buried runs around irrigation lines, beds and patios and restore what we open.
Every new line is pressure-tested before it goes into service, and we tell you up front when a permit is needed.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: Can my gas line handle an outdoor kitchen?
items.preview: Maybe. We calculate the load first.
items.answer: Maybe. We add up the demand of everything on the system and upsize the line if needed.

items.preview: New gas work usually requires one.
items.answer: New gas piping usually requires a permit. We'll explain what applies.

items.q: How deep is a buried gas line?
items.preview: Deep enough to meet code and protected properly.
items.answer: We bury outdoor lines to code depth with the right pipe and protection, and add a shutoff where it surfaces.
Most residential installs take a day, including the pressure test.

items.q: Can you add a gas line for a pool heater?
items.answer: Yes. Pool heaters draw a lot of gas, so we size the line for the heater plus everything else on the system and run it to code.

items.q: What does gas line installation cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the run and the appliance. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the pipe size and the appliance. We quote a flat rate before we start.
